extracted.intended_audience: NLP / machine learning researchers and practitioners working on story generation and natural language generation
extracted.subtask_description: Generate coherent, well-formed stories from a sequence of independent short descriptions (scene/event descriptions). The paper explores posing the task as a translation problem (SMT) and as a sequence-to-sequence deep learning problem and evaluates outputs with machine-translation and summarization metrics on a public dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent story generation from independent descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Task: coherent story generation from independent descriptions, describing a scene or an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to transform incoherent input descriptions (each independently describing aspects of a scene/event) into a single coherent story. The paper frames this as the central desideratum for the system and evaluates approaches on their ability to achieve coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity, originality and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Desiderata: higher levels of creativity, originality and brevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract highlights that effective NLG solutions (or evaluations) for tasks demanding creativity, originality, and brevity are elusive; thus systems should be assessed for these qualities in addition to basic fluency/coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formedness and comprehensiveness (story-likeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce 'well formed comprehensive story like summaries'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs should be well-formed (grammatically and stylistically coherent) and comprehensive in the sense of forming a story-like summary that brings together the independent descriptions into a unified narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: translation framing (SMT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pose story generation as a translation problem and apply phrase-based SMT (PB-SMT) and syntax-based SMT (SYNTAX-SMT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is both a methodological choice and an implicit production criterion: the transformation should be modelled such that incoherent input can be 'translated' into coherent story text. The paper uses two popular SMT variants to implement this framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: sequence-to-sequence deep learning (RNN encoder-decoder)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a deep recurrent neural network architecture that encodes a sequence of variable-length input descriptions into latent representations and decodes them into stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful model should be able to encode variable-length sequences of independent descriptions into meaningful latent representations and decode them into coherent, story-like outputs. Implementation choices (encoder/decoder capacity, handling variable length, training regime) affect meeting this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation with machine translation and summarization metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficacy demonstrated using 'popular machine translation and summarization evaluation metrics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper evaluates generated stories using established automatic metrics from MT and summarization (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics implied though not specified on the page). This implies an evaluation rubric based on n-gram overlap / summarization-oriented measures; however, the abstract does not list specific metric names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a publicly available dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate methods on 'a publicly available dataset'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility and comparability are implied: systems should be evaluated on public data so results can be compared. The page does not name the dataset on the abstract page, but treating the dataset as publicly available is an explicit requirement of the reported experimental setup.
